clinician.trajectory_summary: A 17-year-old male presented with polyurea, polydipsia, general weakness, pallor, bilateral progressive hearing loss since childhood, and lack of weight gain for three years. Initial workup revealed severe hyperglycemia (random blood glucose 407 mg/dL, HbA1c 8.5%). Clinical examination showed a scrotal mass, small penis with enclosed testicles, no pubic or axillary hair (suggesting hypogonadism), short stature, hallux valgus, Boutonniere deformity in toes and hands, and hyperpigmented plaques. Hematological abnormalities were noted, and audiological examination confirmed profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Mutation analysis of SLC29A3 was performed to confirm the diagnosis.

Clinical examination revealed a scrotal mass, a small penis (<0.5 cm) with enclosed testicles, and no pubic or axillary hair, consistent with hypogonadism and scrotal lump.
Hallux valgus and Boutonniere deformity in the toes and hands were observed.
Skin examination revealed hyperpigmented plaques with clear borders.
Audiological examination revealed profound bilateral sensorineural hearing loss.
Mutation analysis of SLC29A3 was performed to confirm the diagnosis.
